findings.reason: without a control (a reference signal known to carry no size information, or a stated margin the winner must clear) the document will report whatever noise ranks first, and the plan's own measurement sections §25 and §29 both declare a control this one omits.
findings.text: §33 declares no negative control and its verdict clause ("It names the signal that best separates pass rate within a requirement, with its bucket counts, or says that none does") is unfalsifiable: with five candidate signals one is always the nominal maximum, and §33 states no effect-size threshold that could make "separates" fail

findings.reason: bins chosen after seeing outcomes can manufacture or hide separation, and a later reader cannot reproduce the table; the plan must fix the bucketing rule (fixed edges or quantiles) or the separating-signal verdict is not evidence.
findings.text: §33's done-when requires "one table per signal: requirement, bucket, rows, passed, median attempts, median review total" for signals that are continuous (clause count, write-path length, estimated_hours, estimated_context) but never states how the buckets are cut, so the binning is left to the node

findings.reason: the window and the referenced matcher disagree, and the plan does not say which wins, so the node may measure the wrong population or fork the matching rule the plan elsewhere insists has one owner.
findings.text: §33's deliverable reads "implement rows over the 30 days to the run, matched as `_candidates_scan` matches them", but `_candidates_scan` bounds its pass with `cutoff = now - timedelta(days=14)` (reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py), so the named mechanism cannot yield the 30-day population — a node reusing it silently measures 14 days, and a node writing its own scan creates a second owner of the matching rule

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_size_class` resolves at `reckon/crew/run_time_profile.py:179`; `_candidates_scan` resolves at `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:257` (cited as 256, a one-line drift the section shares with the unchanged §31/§32 text); `picker_selection.rendered_state` and the `node_definition.{done_when,write_paths,negative_control,estimated_hours}` keys it proposes to read all exist on a ledger row.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §33's done-when names three checks and no negative control, its central verdict ("names the signal that best separates … or says that none does") cannot fail, and it fixes no bucketing rule for its continuous signals, so the measure holds however the data falls and its bins are chosen post hoc.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the research document and its figures sit under `docs/research/` and `docs/figures/`, and the computing script is named from the run directory, all durable paths.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `what-sizes-a-node.html` and the figures directory carry no plan label, stage name or version tag, and no comment states a tracker reference.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §33 fixes a 30-day row window while specifying the rows "matched as `_candidates_scan` matches them", and that function's own cutoff is hard-coded at 14 days, so the mechanism it names does not produce the population the deliverable states.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §33 carries one deliverable (one research document reporting which dispatch-time signal separates outcomes), with §34 explicitly holding the conditioning work.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the changed units add no unmet dependency; §33 (new) measures independent of the picker block refactors, and §34's dependency on §33 is stated in its own prose ("stays deferred until §33 names a signal") with the machine relation to be finalized when its done-when is written.
